title.narrative: International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) Core Support 2024-2026

description.narrative:
ICM Strategic Priorities 2024-2026
Strategic Priority 1: Drive innovation, leadership, and sustainability for the future of midwifery
- Ensure a sustainable ICM, including human, social, economic, and environmental elements.
- Facilitate a responsive ICM that is constantly learning and responding to the needs of its members in new and improved ways.
- Equip Member Associations and midwives across all generations to claim their place as sustainable leaders and secure their roles at decision-making tables and communities, across the midwifery profession both globally and locally, and in aligned sectors.
- Ensure ICM is engaged with donors, partners, governments, and the private sector to provide technical assistance, and leadership in the development and implementation of midwife-led services, new resources and innovations.
- Utilise and promote more digital knowledge management resources to reach and support midwives and their associations at all stages of their professional development globally.
Strategic Priority 2: Support the dissemination and implementation of the Professional Framework for Midwifery
- Promote midwives as autonomous professionals to improve health outcomes for mothers and babies and quality SRMNAH care.
- Describe and advocate for an enabling environment for midwives that facilitates the necessary professional agency, system-level infrastructure, integration, and funding needed for midwives to practise across the full scope of practice of a midwife, as defined by ICM.
- Strengthen midwifery essential competencies, education, regulation and leadership.
- Drive the use of research and evidence for the profession of midwifery and midwife-led continuity of care.
- Elevate the unique role of midwives associations as the voice for midwives and to support and advance the profession.
Strategic Priority 3: Collaborate with partners to grow the movement for midwifery and elevate the role of midwives as competent and respected healthcare providers who put womens voices at the centre.
- Leverage advocacy and communications to influence and educate policymakers and wider audiences about the positive impact of midwives on maternal and newborn health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender equality, in addition to impacts on families and communities.
- Equip midwives and Member Associations with data and tools to effectively advocate for continuity of midwife care, maternal, newborn, sexual and reproductive health and rights.
- Utilise effective and equitable relationships to build and support the profession of midwifery and expand the influence of ICM.
- Support Member Associations to build up partnerships with womens groups and communities.
- Support partnerships between midwives and women.
- Strengthen partnerships between midwives and other stakeholders, including global and national policymakers, other health workers and professionals, other health professional associations and partners across sectors.
Strategic Priority 4: Work in partnership to ensure Member Associations are prepared and well positioned to respond to emergent humanitarian and climate crises.
- Build new partnerships to mitigate the effects of humanitarian and climate crises on women and newborns by advocating to wider audiences on the important role midwives play in crisis situations and securing new funding and partnerships in the humanitarian and climate sectors.
- Establish and secure funding dedicated to providing Member Associations with essential resources (equipment, services, supplies, etc.) in times of humanitarian crisis.
- Enhance Member Association training to better support responses to crises including promoting midwife leadership in national and local preparedness planning and knowledge sharing between MAs.

International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) har ett kärnstöd på 29 000 000 kr under perioden 2024-2026. ICM är ett globalt nätverk som består av mer än hundra nationella och regionala barnmorskeförbund. ICM:s övergripande mål är att varje gravid kvinna ska ha tillgång till barnmorskevård för sig och sitt nyfödda barn. Genom att kapacitetstärka barnmorskor och främja barnmorskeyrket globalt bidrar insatsen till att trygga graviditet och förlossningar, samt att främja SRHR, för alla i hela världen med fokus på de fattigaste länderna.
ICM:s programmatiska arbete fokuserar på barnmorskor, sexuell-, reproduktiv-, mödra-, neonatal-, barn- och ungdomshälsovård (SRMNCAH) och kvinnors- och flickors rättigheter. Sidas kärnstöd under 2020-2023 har varit avgörande för ICMs arbete att stärka organisationen och positionera sig som ledande inom barnmorskeproffessionen. Stödet har resulterat i att ICM nu har en självklar plats i globala sammanhang samt nära samarbeten med UNFPA och WHO. Sidas fortsatta kärnstödfinansiering ger ICM möjligheten att fortsätta bygga upp och stärka sin organisation och kapacitet för att mer effektivt implementera sin strategi. Under 2024 kommer inga Sida medel att vidareförmedlas, men avtalet öppnar för möjligheten för ICM att vidareförmedla om beslutade avtalsvillkor uppfylls.

The International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) has core support of SEK 29,000,000 over the period of 2024-2026. ICM is a global network of more than a hundred national and regional midwifery associations. ICM's overall goal is that every childbearing woman should have access to midwifery care for herself and her newborn child. By strengthening midwives and promoting the global capacity of the midwifery profession, the effort contributes to safe pregnancy and childbirth, as well as promoting SRHR, for everyone but with a focus on the poorest countries.
ICM's programmatic work focuses on midwifery as well as an integrated approach to sexual, reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health care (SRMNCAH) and women's and girls' rights. Sida's core support during 2020-2023 has been decisive for ICM's work to strengthen the organization and position itself as a leader in the midwifery profession. The support has resulted in ICM's obvious place in global contexts relating to midwifery as well as SRHR, and in close collaborations with UNFPA and WHO. Sida's continued core support gives ICM the opportunity to continue building and strengthening its organization and capacity to more effectively implement its strategy. During 2024, no forward funding of Sida funds is allowed. The agreement, however, opens up the possibility for ICM to forward funding if decided contractual conditions are met.

ICM is an accredited non-governmental organisation (NGO) that supports, represents, and works to strengthen professional associations of midwives throughout the world. Organised across six regions (Africa, Americas, Eastern Mediterranean, Europe, Southeast Asia, and Western Pacific) ICM's 139 member associations (MAs) represent over 1 million midwives in 119 countries. In 2024 they have strengthened global positioning of midwifery in different ways:
ICM played a key role in the development and publishing of WHO's position paper and implementation guidance for support to countries to transition to Midwifery Models of Care (MMoC). The position paper was published by WHO in October 2024, setting out the research and evidence to make the case for the transition from existing maternity services to MMoC for safe and efficient care. These models of care are led by autonomous midwives, who provide care to women and newborns through their full scope of practice. The Implementation Guide was subsequently launched at the World Health Assembly in 2025. Significant consultation took place for both documents, and partners collaborated on an advocacy approach to accelerate uptake and support for MMoC globally.
ICM has also played a central role in developing the Global Midwifery Accelerator, in collaboration with UNFPA, WHO, Sida, FCDO, FIGO and UNICEF and many other partners. The Midwifery Accelerator is set to be a powerful advocacy tool designed to amplify the WHO-led Midwifery Models of Care Position Paper and Implementation Guide. The accelerator was launched in April 2025 during the 58th Session of the Commission on Population and Development in NY.
The Alliance to Improve Midwifery Education (AIME) is a consortium of leading global organisations working together to enhance Midwifery Education worldwide and implement and evaluate the effectiveness of programmes to improve quality of midwifery education. ICM is one of the founding partners of AIME together with UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, Laerdal Global Health, the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, Burnet Institute, and Jhpiego. Several seminars led by ICM and UNFPA in the second half of 2024 brought together over 800 global participants from 96 countries. The webinars provided an overview of ICM wealth of resources and tools designed to strengthen midwifery education.
Another of ICM's priority areas is to enhance the capacity of midwifery associations. Through new tools, technical resources, and regional exchanges, ICM contributed to improved organisational capacity of MAs to deliver midwifery services and participate in national health policy environments. For example, Throughout 2024, ICM worked closely with the Bangladesh Midwifery Society (BMS) to strengthen their governance systems and structures. A needs assessment was conducted with BMS to better understand their governance needs. Based on this, an external consultant was engaged to revise the BMS constitution in Bangla and English to better meet their needs. Regular meetings were held with BMS to facilitate this process and to support their procedures around e.g. board elections. ICM also supported BMS with their advocacy work. Despite delays due to a period of political instability in the country, a lot of progress has been made. A number of stakeholder meetings have also been held to address gaps in the provision of midwifery services including with private hospitals to advocate the creation of midwifery positions in these institutions. ?
ICM has worked alongside the Zambian Ministry of Health, the Midwifery Association of Zambia (MAZ), and key stakeholders to advance and sustain ensure midwifery-led models of care, aiming to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and appeal of healthcare services. Significant milestones have been achieved including embedding midwifery priorities in the National Health Strategic Plan and creating the first National Nurse and Midwife Strategic Plan.
The ICM Essential Competencies for Midwifery Practice (2024) outlines the minimum set of knowledge, skills and professional behaviours required to use the designation of midwife, as defined by ICM, when entering midwifery practice. The Competencies are essential and represent those that should be an expected outcome of midwifery pre-service education. In 2023, ICM undertook an extensive consultation to update the Essential Competencies for Midwifery Practice as part of their our five year review cycle. The updated Competencies were approved by the ICM Council in June 2024, and launched in August. The latest iteration includes the addition of category 2, focusing specifically on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), contraception, and pre-conception care.
In a turbulent world ICM with many challenges affecting the work of midwives, another priority for ICM is to improve the crisis preparedness of midwives. Recognizing that climate change is already impacting sexual and reproductive health and Right globally ICM support MAs to place greater emphasis on readiness for humanitarian and climate related crises to contribute to more resilient health systems in fragile settings. This is one of the core priorities of the 2024-2026 ICM strategy. They conducted a survey in 2024 to examine midwives engagement in clinical and advocacy efforts and whether they see their profession as playing a role in addressing these challenges. In the report, 75% of midwives stated that climate change is harming the communities they serve, with rising rates of preterm births, food insecurity, and restricted access to care during disasters like floods. Midwives in communities witness and respond to these effects from extreme weather events to displacement and food insecurity. However, increasing climate-related disasters are straining health care systems, deepening health inequities, and limiting their ability to provide essential care. The survey findings highlighted midwives critical role in climate-related health emergencies, often serving as first responders to crises such as floods restricting maternity care access or extreme heat worsening pregnancy complications. Despite this, their work is becoming more challenging, threatening the well-being of the communities they serve.
Some of the challenges that are reported to affect the results of ICM are the financial constraints within ICM and the broader global health and humanitarian sector as well as the increasing global restrictions on SRHR that limits policy space and require continued advocacy.
